glosses: To open.

examples.text: Some vacancies have opened up due to retirements.
Open up the door!
The executive pay gap is opening up again.
Wilshire then opened up Everton's defence, but Van Persie lifted his finish over the onrushing Howard and also over the bar.

glosses: To widen.

examples.text: The corridor gradually opened up into a triangular room.

glosses: To reveal oneself; to share personal information about oneself; to become communicative.

examples.text: After three hours of questioning, he finally opened up.

glosses: To commence firing weapons.

examples.text: As the convoy entered the pass, we opened up on them with everything we had.

glosses: To rain.

examples.text: The sky has really opened up. I've never seen this much rain!

glosses: To begin running, driving, travelling, etc., at maximum (or faster) speed.

examples.text: The pigeon is moving as before with unhurried haste. [...] But it must be all out. If it wasn't, then it would open up and get away from that shadow of death behind it.

Then we simply crawled onwards to Tebay, and not until well on to the 1 in 75 did the driver open up; the result was no greater drop than from 57 at Tebay to a sustained 40 m.p.h. up the last mile to Shap Summit.

examples.text: In stage acting, we are frequently asked to cheat out to the audience by opening up our body positions so that we are something halfway between facing them and our partner.
